title: Trees
summary: A tree stores values in parent and child nodes, with one root at the top.
refresher: A tree node stores a value and links to child nodes. Traversal means visiting nodes in a clear order, such as root-left-right or level by level.

sections.title: Tree node shape
sections.summary: A binary tree node has a value, a left child, and a right child.

blocks.body: A tree starts at the root. From there, each node can point to children. A binary tree has at most two children: left and right.

blocks.caption: This is the basic binary tree node shape.

choices: The first/top node of the tree
blocks.why: Traversal usually starts at the root, then moves to children.

sections.title: Traversal order
sections.summary: Traversal is the order you visit nodes.

blocks.body: Depth-first traversal follows one branch before backing up. Breadth-first traversal visits nodes level by level using a queue.

blocks.prompt: Which structure helps visit a tree level by level?
blocks.why: A queue keeps older discovered nodes first, which matches level order.
